critical_findings.title: RLS authorises from a user-writable JWT claim (privilege escalation)
critical_findings.status: NOT_TESTED (confirmed from code and design; not exploited)
critical_findings.detail: Every RLS policy across all 37 migrations reads auth.jwt() -> 'user_metadata' ->> 'role'. Zero policies use app_metadata. user_metadata derives from auth.users.raw_user_meta_data, which an authenticated browser session can write via supabase.auth.updateUser({data:{role:'branch_manager'}}). Any employee could therefore grant themselves manager privileges at the database layer.
critical_findings.not_exploited_reason: No disposable test account was available and operating rule 10 prohibits testing privilege escalation against a real account. The project's own test suite declines this test for the same reason.
critical_findings.remediation: Migrate every RLS policy to auth.jwt() -> 'app_metadata' ->> 'role'. supabase/functions/admin-users/index.ts already writes app_metadata.role on user create and update; nothing currently reads it. Backfill existing users and require re-login.

critical_findings.title: Document service authorises on an unsigned client-supplied header
critical_findings.detail: backend/services/auth.py checks membership of the X-User-Role header in a two-element set. There is no JWT verification and no binding to a Supabase session, although the frontend does forward a bearer token that the server ignores. Verified in-process: no header -> 403, risk_department -> 403, audit_department -> 403, branch_employee -> 400 (access granted). CORS is allow_origins=['*'].
critical_findings.remediation: Verify the Supabase JWT server-side and derive the role from the verified token; restrict CORS to known origins.
